taxonomy.label: Framing failure
taxonomy.description: The work answered a different question than the one that mattered.

taxonomy.label: Source of truth mismatch
taxonomy.description: The wrong source was treated as authoritative.

taxonomy.label: Missing gate
taxonomy.description: A readiness or approval check was skipped or absent.

taxonomy.label: Late data
taxonomy.description: The signal arrived too late or was already stale.

taxonomy.label: Threshold mismatch
taxonomy.description: The cutoff, limit, or boundary was chosen poorly.

taxonomy.label: Scope mismatch
taxonomy.description: The task was too broad, too narrow, or outside the actual scope.

taxonomy.label: Ownership gap
taxonomy.description: Responsibility or handoff was unclear.

taxonomy.label: Calibration drift
taxonomy.description: The confidence model, threshold, or estimate drifted away from reality.

taxonomy.label: Timing error
taxonomy.description: The action happened too early, too late, or with the wrong latency.

taxonomy.label: Tooling gap
taxonomy.description: The path, command, or tool was missing or broken.

taxonomy.label: State drift
taxonomy.description: The active state diverged from the expected state.

taxonomy.label: Implicit assumption
taxonomy.description: A hidden assumption was treated as a fact.

lessons.title: Yuri readiness gates must be live, not declarative

tags.label: Implicit assumption
tags.description: A hidden assumption was treated as a fact.

lessons.title: Yuri readiness gates must be live, not declarative
questions: What happened?
The council audit exposed a false-readiness pattern: tests could pass while build, live memory health, GitNexus status, launchd runtime, and skill registry drift were failing or unverified.
What was the real question?
Can Yuri prove operational readiness from deterministic local commands and canonical memory state?
What question did I answer instead?
Whether a written plan described the right architecture.
What did I assume without checking?
That plan status, unit-test status, and current runtime status were equivalent.
